name: Cell Seeding Density Calculator
seoTitle: Cell Seeding Density Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Seeding density is the number of cells per unit area or volume you start a culture with. Free cell seeding density calculator: enter your values and get cells
summary:
Seeding density is the number of cells per unit area or volume you start a culture with. It returns cells per vessel, suspension to pipette per vessel, cells needed in total and medium to add per vessel, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Get it wrong and the experiment either takes a week to reach confluence or is confluent the next morning. This calculator turns a target density into the volume of suspension to pipette and the medium to add. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Cell Seeding Density
sections.html:
Cells per vessel = target density × growth area; volume = cells per vessel ÷ stock concentration

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
targetcells per cm² you want to start withcells/cm²
areagrowth area of one flask or wellcm²
concstock concentrationcells/mL

sections.title: How do I use the Cell Seeding Density?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: stock concentration of 1,500,000 cells/mL, target density of 20,000 cells/cm², growth area per vessel of 25 cm², number of vessels of 1, final volume per vessel of 5 mL.

Substituting them into the formula gives cells per vessel of 500,000 cells, suspension to pipette per vessel of 0.3333 mL, cells needed in total of 500,000 cells, medium to add per vessel of 4.67 mL.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
5 000 – 20 000 /cm²Sparsecloning, single-cell work
20 000 – 50 000 /cm²Standardroutine passage of most lines
above 50 000 /cm²Densefast experiments, or a line that needs contact

  • Seeding density sets the time to confluence: doubling the density roughly halves it, which is often easier than changing the medium.

  • Growth area is the number that matters for adherent cells; the flask volume is just what fits over it.

  • For a first passage of a new line, seed two densities and keep the one that looks right on day two.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Using the flask's nominal volume instead of its growth area.
  • Forgetting that the medium added dilutes the density — you seed cells into the final volume.
  • Seeding dead cells: always work from the live-cell count, not the total.

faq.q: How many cells should I seed in a 6-well plate?
faq.a: A well is about 9.6 cm², so 20 000 cells/cm² is roughly 190 000 cells per well.

faq.q: Does seeding density affect the experiment?
faq.a: It changes growth rate, confluency timing and sometimes differentiation, so keep it constant across arms.

faq.q: What does the Cell Seeding Density actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns cells per vessel, suspension to pipette per vessel, cells needed in total and medium to add per vessel. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
